subject: Making predictions changes posterior coefficient estimates

messages.author: 472cc3e7f6c1577c
messages.subject: Making predictions changes posterior coefficient estimates
parts:
Hi all,
I'd be massively appreciative of any help with a weird problem I'm having using INLA.

The problem is, that when I have NA's in my dependent variable (so that I can make predictions for these points), the coefficient estimates change. I thought that including points for prediction should not effect estimation of coefficients?

I've attached some code and toy data. When I run these models, I get the following coefficient estimates (here, testModel_1 is observed points only, testModel_2 is with additional points I want to predict):
summary(testModel_1)
...
Fixed effects:
                  mean      sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant     mode kld
(Intercept)   -23.3015 10.0147   -46.4345 -21.7834    -7.8407 -18.0330   0
bioclim1        2.2509  1.3855     0.1035   2.0465     5.4444   1.5455   0
I(bioclim1^2)  -0.0802  0.0480    -0.1904  -0.0733    -0.0051  -0.0566   0

summary(testModel_2)
...
Fixed effects:
                  mean      sd 0.025quant 0.5quant 0.975quant     mode kld
(Intercept)   -22.2029 10.0185   -45.2643 -20.7322    -6.5837 -17.1620   0
bioclim1        2.1718  1.3859    -0.0194   1.9798     5.3460   1.5243   0
I(bioclim1^2)  -0.0796  0.0480    -0.1886  -0.0734    -0.0025  -0.0590   0

I'm running R 3.4.1 and INLA_17.07.20-1, on an ubuntu 16.04 system. Please let me know if any further information is required.

I'd be hugely grateful for any help with this matter!
Dave

messages.author: f66907f526d3c7bf
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Making predictions changes posterior coefficient estimates
parts:
The problem looks like numerical instability (I'm sure Håvard can
explain more). The solution is to scale your variables (and also make
sure the number of successes is an integer!). This also shortens your
credible intervals, which makes all the gods of marginalisation happy:

library(INLA)
library(data.table)

# read in toy data
allData <- fread("toyData.csv")
allData$N <- allData$sp1*allData$nTrials
allData$bioclim1.sc <- scale(allData$bioclim1)

# subset data for points where we have observations
obsData <- allData[!is.na(sp1), ]

# define formula
formula <- N ~ bioclim1.sc + I(bioclim1.sc^2)

testModel_1 <- inla(formula,
data = obsData,
family = "binomial",
Ntrials = obsData$nTrials,
control.predictor = list(compute = T),
control.compute = list(dic = T))

testModel_2 <- inla(formula,
data = allData,
family = "binomial",
Ntrials = allData$nTrials,
control.predictor = list(compute = T),
control.compute = list(dic = T))


summary(testModel_1)
summary(testModel_2)

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Making predictions changes posterior coefficient estimates
parts:
this is my conclusion to. the response is the number of successes, not
divided by nTrials. I also have the question if this is really what you
want, since you have mostly zeros in the response, and very very little
information in your data...

H
